steps.body: Scattered things are hardest to count — nothing separates counted from uncounted. The oldest trick fixes it: mark each one as its number is said.
steps.narration: Scattered things are hardest to count — nothing separates counted from uncounted. The oldest trick fixes it: mark each one as its number is said.

widget.prompt: 9 stickers are scattered. Mark each as you count — a counter per mark.

commonCounts.feedback: A clean sticker is hiding somewhere; unmarked means uncounted.
A sticker was marked twice; each mark must land on a clean one.

widget.missFeedback: Mark one sticker per number; when no clean stickers remain, the last number is the answer.
widget.successFeedback: Nine marks, nine stickers — the mess never stood a chance.

predict.prompt: Counting scattered stickers without marking — the danger is…
predict.reveal: With nothing separating counted from uncounted, both mistakes come easily.

cml.actionGoal: Pair each object with exactly one number and trust the last number said for kch count scattered.
invariants: A count pairs objects with number words one to one, and its last word names the whole group — which is why order, spacing, and arrangement can change without changing the answer for kch count scattered.
misconceptions: Skipping or double-counting an object, recounting when nothing changed, or believing a spread-out group holds more.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more object joined the group, what would the last counting word become?

widget.prompt: The stickers are scattered everywhere. What is the best counting plan?

options.label: Mark or move each one as it is counted
options.feedback: Correct — marking separates the counted from the uncounted, which is what scattered groups make hard.

options.label: Count fast before they move
options.feedback: Speed invites skips and repeats; scattered things need marking, not hurrying.

options.label: Count only the easy ones
options.feedback: Every sticker needs a number, or the final count answers a different question.

options.label: Guess from how big the mess looks
options.feedback: A guess is not a count; the mess can look big with few stickers or small with many.

steps.body: Use a different representation to test the same idea.

widget.prompt: Organize a count of scattered stickers.

items.label: Stop when every sticker is marked
Say the next number and mark it

misorderFeedback.feedback: Begin with the starting set or marker before you count or stop.

widget.missFeedback: Use this order: Find an unmarked sticker, then Say the next number and mark it, then Stop when every sticker is marked.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — each visible mark separates counted stickers from waiting stickers.

widget.prompt: Noor counts her blocks: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. How many blocks does she have?

options.feedback: Correct — the last number said, 5, tells how many blocks there are in all.
The count stops at 5; saying one more number would count a block that is not there.
That stops one number early — every block gets exactly one number, ending at 5.
That runs two past the count; the last number spoken is the answer, and it was 5.

widget.prompt: Start at 9 and count on 3. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 11 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 12.
13 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 3 hops from 9 to land on 12.

widget.missFeedback: Start at 9 and count on 3: you land on 12.
widget.successFeedback: 9 and 3 more is 12 — counting on continues the count instead of starting over.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 3 counts are needed to reach 12.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 3 numbers, on 12.
